subject: Deployment mode recommendation — next steps & sizing
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: John Lee <john.lee@brightline.com>
Cc: Ava Thomson <ava.thomson@brightline.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Oct 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: deployment mode recs + data we need

Hi John / Ava —

Thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment on the Hosted vs Dedicated question you raised. TL;DR: for a short pilot, Hosted API is fastest to get started; for predictable p99 latency at scale we should evaluate a Dedicated pool (or Dedicated + burst).

What I heard on the call
- Peak burst (short duration): ~100–140 QPS
- Sustained average: ~20–40 QPS
- Typical generation size: 120–350 tokens per request (median ~180)
- Latency targets: p95 ~300ms, p99 <= 800ms for end-to-end generation
- Data residency: US-only; no on-prem requirement for pilot
- Security: standard SOC2 + encryption at rest; will confirm with your security team if anything extra is needed

Questions / asks for sizing and final recommendation
1) Can you send a 24–72h trace or summary of request rate by minute (even anonymized) so we can simulate queueing and batching effects?
2) Any hard SLA or contractual latency requirement for go-live?
3) Will you need private network/VPC connectivity for the POC?

Initial recommendation (to enable an informed decision quickly)
- Pilot (2–4 weeks): Hosted API with reserved throughput credits and KV-prefix caching. Low friction, fastest time-to-value.
- Production (if p99 matters at sustained scale): Dedicated pool sized to your sustained QPS with headroom (example: 3–5x sustained slots depending on model/quantization). Dedicated gives consistent p99 and predictable billing.

Next steps I propose
- You share the traffic trace and any security checklist (I can send our standard questionnaire)
- I’ll attach a quick sizing spreadsheet (example numbers) and a mutual action plan so we can agree on deliverables + timeline
- Schedule a short infra sync (30–45m) with your engineering team — Ben (cc) from our side will join to discuss latencies/bench plans

I’ve attached: redwood-mvp-sizing.xlsx (back-of-envelope), mutual-action-plan.pdf (M.A.P)

If all looks good, we can run a 1–2 week latency-focused POC on Hosted to validate numbers and then spin up Dedicated capacity if needed.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once you confirm availability.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez

Thanks Sergio — helpful summary. A few data points from our side to fill in the gaps:

- Recent production snapshot (typical weekday):
  • Peak 1-minute: 120 QPS (rare spikes to ~140 for flash sales)
  • 95th percentile: ~40 QPS sustained
  • Average: 18–25 QPS
- Average generation: 190 tokens, with a long tail up to ~450 tokens on some prompts
- Latency requirement: end-to-end p95 target <= 300ms, p99 we’d like <= 800ms; if p99 cannot be met we'd need automated fallbacks (like degraded model or shorter context)
- Security: SOC2 is fine for now; we have a vendor review but no additional controls needed for pilot
- Contracting: we’ll want an option for Reserved Dedicated for production if Hosted POC shows need; curious about burst behavior while Dedicated warms up

Questions for you:
1) Can you provide a ballpark monthly cost delta between Hosted pilot (with reserved credits for QPS) vs Dedicated pool sized for sustained 40 QPS?
2) Does Dedicated support instant burst (e.g., autoscaling within minutes) or is there a warm-up?

We can share the 48h request logs (anonymized) — I’ll upload to the Drive link you provided. Also, would like Ben on the call for any kernel/quantization tradeoffs.

John

Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment mode recs + data we need

John — great, thanks for the numbers, that helps a lot. I pulled a quick back-of-envelope in the attached sheet. Short answers to your questions below, and I’ve added Ben (Infrastructure) and Monica (Customer Success) to coordinate the POC + contracting timeline.

Ballpark cost delta (very rough; will refine after we size kernel/model):
- Hosted pilot with reserved credits to cover expected 120 QPS spikes (throttled by quota otherwise): estimated ~$12k–18k/month depending on token volume and caching efficiency
- Dedicated pool sized for sustained 40 QPS (with headroom for autoscaling to 120 brief spikes): estimated committed cost ~$28k–35k/month; burst policies can add incremental cost when using burst capacity

Dedicated behavior notes:
- Dedicated offers fast warm-up for KV cache; for cold start there is some model init latency (~2–6s) but per-request p99 for sustained traffic is far more predictable than Hosted noisy neighbors
- Autoscaling: configurable — we can set aggressive scale-up (minutes) or conservative policies. For strict p99 we typically recommend steady Dedicated with short burst capacity for flash events.

Immediate next steps I’ll take this afternoon:
- Drop the MAP and sizing spreadsheet into the Drive you shared
- Propose 30–45m infra sync (Ben + Monica + Sergio) to walk through latency test plan and confirm Drive upload
- Provide a sample SOW/payment approach for Dedicated reserved capacity once we agree on production sizing

Attached: redwood-mvp-sizing.xlsx (spreadsheet), mutual-action-plan.pdf

Thanks — I’ll pencil in a couple times.

Sergio
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
